instructions: Up to 3 days ahead, heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Brush the olive oil into all 12 cups of a muffin pan.
Chop 1 cup of the baby spinach, lightly packed.
Finely dice the red pepper and the green pepper.
Quarter 1 cup of the cherry tomatoes.
Divide the spinach, peppers and tomatoes between the 12 cups. They should be about two thirds full.
Crack 6 of the eggs into a large jug with a spout. Separate the last 4 eggs and add only the whites to the jug.
Add the 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp basil, 1/4 tsp oregano and a pinch of pepper. Whisk until there are no streaks of white left.
Pour the egg over the vegetables until each cup is about three quarters full. Sprinkle the feta over the tops.
Bake for 24 to 28 minutes, until they're puffed and the centers don't wobble when you shake the pan. This makes 12 egg bites.
Let them cool in the pan for 5 minutes. Run a small knife around each one and lift it out onto a rack to cool completely.

They keep in the fridge for up to 3 days in a sealed container, or in the freezer for up to 3 months, each one wrapped. In the morning, microwave two for about 30 seconds, or 1 to 2 minutes from frozen.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the egg bites up to 3 days ahead and keep them in the fridge.
method_notes: All three bake whisked eggs over spinach in a greased muffin pan at 350°F, with feta in or on top. Well Plated (the lead) uses 6 whole eggs plus 4 whites, adds peppers, tomatoes, basil and oregano and bakes them for 24 to 28 minutes. Love and Lemons blends the eggs with cottage cheese and only suggests feta on top, and I Heart Vegetables keeps it to spinach, feta, eggs and a little milk. This one follows the lead's 12 bites as written.
